title: Multiplication table with while
description: Display the 7 times table using a while loop, from 1 to 10.
hints: Initialize i = 1 and the condition is i <= 10
Do not forget i++ at the end of the body to avoid an infinite loop
solutionExplanation: The counter i starts at 1 and is incremented in each iteration. The condition i <= 10 guarantees exactly 10 iterations. Without the i++ the loop would be infinite.

title: Guess the number with limited attempts
description: Simulate a game where the user tries to guess a secret number between 1 and 100. Use do-while to allow up to 5 attempts, showing 'higher' or 'lower' clues.
hints: Compare the attempt with the secret to give the clue
solutionExplanation: do-while guarantees at least one attempt. We keep an attempt counter and a match boolean. The compound condition allows exiting when matching or when the 5 attempts are used up. The higher/lower clues guide the user.
expectedOutput:
Attempt 1: 50 - the secret is higher
Attempt 2: 80 - the secret is lower
Attempt 3: 70 - the secret is higher
Attempt 4: 75 - the secret is lower
Attempt 5: 73 - Correct! 🎉

title: Square root calculation with the Babylonian method
description: Calculate the square root of a number using the Babylonian method (Newton): iterate improving an estimate until the difference between iterations is less than 0.0001. The number of iterations is unknown.
hints: Use Math.abs(nueva - estimacion) to measure the change between iterations
The while condition: the difference >= epsilon
Remember to update estimacion = nueva at the end of each iteration
solutionExplanation: The Babylonian method refines the estimate in each iteration with the formula (e + n/e)/2. We use while(true) with an exit condition based on convergence (change < epsilon), a classic case of an indeterminate loop where the number of iterations is not known in advance.
